messages:
jordan_customer: Hey team — we just provisioned a service-account API key via SCIM for an automation user and every request returns 401 invalid_api_key. The key shows up in the Console as 'Created' and I can copy it. Example: curl to /v1/embeddings -> 401. Any ideas?

maya_support: Sorry you're blocked, @jordan_customer. Can you paste the curl you used (redact full key except last 6 chars) and confirm which header you put the key in? Also last successful timestamp would help. :thinking:

jordan_customer: Sure — here's the repro (redacted):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -H "Authorization: ApiKey sa_Abc12345efgh" \\n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Response: 401 {"error":"invalid_api_key"}
Last tried: 2025-11-02T14:12:08Z

maya_support: Ah — quick note: our docs recommend `Authorization: Bearer <key>` for service keys. Can you try with Bearer and paste the last 6 chars of the key (e.g., `...45efgh`) so we can look it up in the backend?
jordan_customer: Tried Bearer too, still 401. Last 6 chars: 45efgh.

alex_engineer: tagging infra_oncall — I pulled the key index for last6=45efgh. Key record exists but auth_index shows state=staged, owner_active=false. That explains 401 even though Console shows "Created". SCIM created the key before the user/service account finished SSO/SCIM activation, so the auth-layer rejects requests until owner_active flips true.

sync_bot: key_sync: key=sa_Abc12345efgh status=queued attempts=0 reason="owner_not_active"

infra_oncall: Thanks @alex_engineer — looks like a race between SCIM provisioner and the key-indexer. Two immediate options for customer: 1) Regenerate the key from Console (new key will be reprocessed and should become active), or 2) Wait ~30-90s for the sync job to pick up the owner activation and flip the key to active. We can also trigger a manual resync from the admin console if you want.

jordan_customer: We need it live now — regenerated key and that one worked immediately. Thanks.

maya_support: Great. Root cause summary for the ticket: service-account key created via SCIM landed in the key table before the identity was fully active; auth indexer treated owner as inactive -> 401 invalid_api_key. Workarounds: regenerate or trigger manual resync.

alex_engineer: Follow-ups for the infra team: add a guard to the Console to hide keys until owner_active=true, or have the SCIM workflow block key creation until activation completes. Also add a small retry/resync hook after SCIM completes so customers don't hit this transient 401. Filed infra issue INFRA-2345.

infra_oncall: Noted INFRA-2345. I'll add a metric to track "key_activation_lag" and a dashboard alert if > 5% of SCIM keys take > 60s to activate.

maya_support: Closing note to @jordan_customer — glad regen fixed it. If you see it again, reply here and we'll trigger a resync for you. :thumbsup:
